newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans sink to lower closes on China, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans sink to lower closes on China, funds.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures tumbled to lower closes on active fund selling amid news that up to one million tonnes of soybean meal was clogging Chinese ports, traders said.
"That's what took us down from the highs. This isn't friendly," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "They (China) are loaded down."
Traders in Shanghai told Reuters that soymeal demand has dropped and buyers are stuck with meal they cannot move.
The news was bearish for U.S. soybean markets because it suggested a major buyer of U.S. supplies would be out of the market until stockpiles dwindled, traders said.
South American weather received mixed reviews as some forecasters predicted widespread rains in soybean regions this week while other suggested rains would be scattered.

Funds were active sellers, accounting for at least 10 million bushels. Traders said Refco Inc and Merrill Lynch each sold four million bushels March and Dean Witter sold two million March. Cargill Investor Services, Griffin Trading and Smith Barney were also sellers of March, traders said.
Soybeans closed 9-1/2 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower with March down 6-1/4 at $7.40-1/2.
Volume was estimated by the CBOT at 45,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 38,046 contracts. ((Emily Kaiser 312-408-8749))
